text:
ops-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT: Latency SLO breach (p95/p99) detected for dedicated-prod-usw2 pool. Alert: SLO:latency.p99 > 2s for 3m. Paging on-call.

pagerduty-bot: Paging devon (on-call). Priority: P1.

devon: on it, just saw the page. joining. Any customer reports?

maria: customer-facing tickets: 2 customers reported streaming stalls and partial responses. They're showing high p99 and timeouts on long chat sessions.

devon: pulling metrics now.

devon: cpu/gpu util for dedicated-prod-usw2: GPUs pinned at ~98% across pool, queue depth spiking. p95 ~ 700ms -> 1.1s, p99 jumping to 2.8s.

maria: this looks like a burst event — traffic spike at 03:12 UTC.

irene: logs from autoscaler show scale decision delayed:
```
2026-03-14T03:12:10Z autoscaler INFO desired_replicas=40 current_replicas=20 reason=queue_depth_threshold
2026-03-14T03:12:20Z autoscaler WARN scale_cooldown active, skip_scale
2026-03-14T03:12:50Z autoscaler INFO pending_warmup=20
```

irene: cooldown prevented immediate scale up; warmup latency for new replicas ~45-60s.

devon: queue_depth metric: dedicated-prod-usw2/queue_depth = 540 at peak. Average token-rate per request also increased.

ops-bot: Annotated affected routes: /v1/generate (streaming), /v1/chat/stream. Impact: increased tail latency and streaming stalls.

sam: I'm available to take oncall handoff in 12m if this goes long.

devon: quick mitigation plan: 1) enable manual burst capacity (if available) 2) route lower-priority tenants to hosted fallback 3) drop max_stream_window or shorten chunk size 4) temporarily tighten per-tenant qps.

maria: I can notify account CSMs for the two impacted customers. Also prepare incident banner if service-affecting continues.

devon: trying manual scale: `redwoodctl pool scale --pool dedicated-prod-usw2 --replicas 60 --force`

deploy-bot: Received scale request. Initiating provisioning of 40 replicas. Estimated warmup: 50-70s.

devon: while replicas boot, enabling routing fallback. `routing set policy dedicated-prod-usw2 -> hosted-fallback` (for non-SLA tenants)

irene: applied temporary routing rule to divert 18% of traffic (best-effort) to hosted variants to relieve queue.

sam: monitoring p99; any streaming-specific metrics?

devon: yes: stream_chunk_latency p95 jumped 900ms -> 1.6s, observed frequent `kv-cache-miss` for warmed sessions which exacerbates tail.

maria: customers reported partial streams (client saw EOF) — looks like long-lived streams dropped when queue hit threshold.

devon: root cause timeline hypothesis: sudden burst saturates dedicated pool -> queue depth grows -> autoscaler sees spike but cooldown prevents immediate scale -> new replicas take ~1m to warm up and load model -> during warmup, continuous batching and KV cache misses cause streaming stalls and tail latency spikes -> p99 breaches.

irene: autoscaler logs show cooldown triggered by back-to-back scale events earlier (03:00 and 03:05), which prevented scale at 03:12. We should revisit cooldown heuristics.

devon: mitigation update: forced replicas have reached 55/60; new replicas are coming online, started model load. Token throughput increasing.

ops-bot: Noted mitigation steps in incident timeline.

maria: CSMs notified. Customer A indicates degraded but usable UX; Customer B requests ETA and is threatening rollback.

devon: temporary config applied to reduce `streaming.window_size` from 8 to 4 for all non-SLA tenants to reduce per-request token pressure.

sam: I'm taking over active incident coordination from devon in 10m — preparing handoff.

devon: handoff notes: forced scale in progress, routing fallback applied, stream_window reduced, per-tenant qps tightened (token_bucket=0.8). Watch p99 and queue_depth. Alerts: SLO:latency.p99 and dedicated-prod-usw2/queue_depth.

sam: acknowledged. I will own communications and next remediation.

devon: small note — KV cache warmup strategy is suboptimal when adding many replicas; new replicas cold cause extra latency. We should consider prewarmed images for burst capacity.

irene: capturing action item: explore prewarmed replica pool and cooldown exceptions for burst events.

deploy-bot: Scale complete: replicas=60. Model load success on 56/60.

ops-bot: SLO status: p99 trending down from 2.8s -> 1.4s after routing fallback and scale. Continue monitoring for 15m.

maria: customers updated: Customer B accepted temporary mitigation, asked for postmortem and SLA credit if recurrence.

sam: next steps: 1) keep existing mitigations for 15 minutes, 2) start postmortem draft (owner: irene), 3) engineering action: adjust autoscaler cooldown policy + add prewarmed replicas (owner: devon).

irene: starting postmortem doc now, will include timeline and metric embeds.

devon: close note — consider adding early-warning metric: queue_depth_derivative to catch very sharp spikes and allow emergency scale override.

ops-bot: Incident state: mitigated -> monitoring. Please update incident tracker. :white_check_mark:

sam: taking over communications thread. Thanks all.

pagerduty-bot: Incident P1 acknowledged by sam. Recording on-call handoff.

maria: will draft customer-facing summary and send in 30m.

irene: assigning follow-ups: `#1 autoscaler cooldown tuning` -> devon, `#2 prewarm pool prototype` -> devon+eng-runtime, `#3 postmortem & RCA` -> irene.

sam: logging final metrics snapshot for postmortem: `p95=560ms p99=1.2s queue_depth_peak=540 replicas_before=20 replicas_after=60 warmup_secs=55`

ops-bot: Incident closed for paging. Monitoring period: 15m. If regressions occur, new incident will be opened.

devon: thanks team. I’ll sync with infra tomorrow to plan a prewarm runbook.

maria: thanks — closing thread for now.
